subject: Q3 lighthouse objectives — endorsement request and risk triage
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Q3 lighthouse objectives — endorsement request and risk triage

Team — attaching the working "Lighthouse" slate for Q3 and a short risk appendix (two small attachments). Goal is to lock owner-level endorsement today so we can publish the QBR packet on Wednesday. Quick summary below and asks: 

- Purpose: set 3 cross-org lighthouse objectives that guide Dedicated, Hosting, and Optimize workstreams. These are intentionally narrow and measurable.
- Asks: please review owner metrics in tab 2 and either 'endorse' or call out a hard blocker by 5pm PT. If you endorse, reply with a single line "ENDORSE" + any open dependencies.
- If you have a resource ask (capital or headcount) escalate inline and flag which objective it affects.
- I'll host a 30-minute triage at 4:30pm PT if there are unresolved items.

Key change candidates compared to the draft you saw last week:
- Reduce quantization rollout target from 30% to 25% of traffic for safety testing windows (see rationale, pg 3).
- Add a customer-facing latency SLO baseline for Redwood Dedicated (95th pct under 120ms).

Attachments: Q3-Lighthouse-Slate.xlsx (owner metrics tab) | Q3-Risk-Appendix.pdf (short risk table).

Next steps: owners reply with endorsement or blocker; I'll collate and publish the packet.

Thanks —
Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Strategy & Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Q3 lighthouse objectives — endorsement request and risk triage

Irene — thanks for the draft and the clear ask. Quick note from infra/serving: the 25% quantization rollout still risks exposing a 3–5% accuracy delta on long-context LLMs for some enterprise workloads. Proposal: keep rollout cap at 20% for the first 6 weeks, then re-evaluate with the eval harness (we have the eval set ready).

If everyone is comfortable with the staged approach I will add a gating step in the rollout playbook (metric: generation-regression < 1.5% on our eval set).

Endorse: yes (with staged quantization change)

Quick operational note: the Dedicated latency SLO is fine as a baseline, but we need a one-time budget to put an observability dashboard in place (2 FTE-weeks from Observability team or a short contractor). That ask is in the risk appendix but I'm repeating it here because it affects delivery sequencing.

Also proposing a 30-minute dry run of the QBR packet with the execs on Tuesday morning (Aug 18, 9:00am PT) — Lauren, can you confirm availability?

Thanks all — recording decisions below and next steps.

Decisions:
- Owners: Q3 lighthouse slate is endorsed (Karthik/Hannah/Marissa/Lauren).
- Quantization rollout: staged cap at 20% for first 6 weeks; gating metric: generation-regression < 1.5% on eval harness. (Karthik to own gating step.)
- Observability dashboard: approved one-time budget; Hannah to coordinate resources (2 FTE-weeks or contractor).

Next steps:
- I will publish the finalized QBR packet (drive link) by Tue 8:30am PT.
- Lauren: confirm exec dry run availability (Hannah suggested Tue Aug 18, 9:00am PT).
- Karthik: post the gating step into the rollout playbook and link to the eval runbook.
- Marissa: loop in CS on customer-facing talking points and the Acme Analytics-specific note.
- Legal: contracts@external-legal.com, please acknowledge the latency SLO language; Nora (Acme) is cc'd for visibility.

Attachments published with final packet: Q3-Lighthouse-Slate.xlsx, Q3-Risk-Appendix.pdf
